item.title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm \mu m$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0${\AA}, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620{\AA} on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$\alpha$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$\alpha$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.
item.dc:creator: Mason S. Huberty, Claudia Scarlata, Matthew J. Hayes, Alaina Henry, Danielle A. Berg, Vieri Cammelli, Richard Ellis, Anne E. Jaskot, Yu-Heng Lin, Vihang Mehta, Matilde Mingozzi, Pierluigi Monaco, Alberto Saldana-Lopez, Aayush Saxena, Jonathan C. Tan, Alice Young

item.title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2610.12591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.
item.dc:creator: Omima Osman, Gabriella De Lucia, Andreas. L. Faisst, Lizhi Xie, Fabio Fontanot, Michaela Hirschmann

item.title: Exploring Case B I: The Footprints of Hidden Radiation Fields in H I Balmer Decrements
item.description: arXiv:2610.12715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Theory predicts that H I emission from photoionized clouds should lie close to the Case B limit established by Menzel and Baker, and observations of nearby nebulae have largely confirmed this expectation. However, recent observations of more distant high-redshift systems have revealed a small fraction with striking departures from Case B. What additional physics might be at work in these objects? This paper is part of a series exploring the physical processes that can produce such departures. In Paper I (D26), we show that Case B remains remarkably robust over a broad range of physical conditions, consistent with observations of nearby nebulae. Here, we explore one additional ingredient: a soft, non-ionizing radiation field. Such a continuum can strongly perturb the Balmer spectrum. The largest effects occur for radiation fields resembling log(Teff K)\sim 3.2-4.2 blackbodies, where photoexcitation from the metastable 2s level alters the hydrogen level populations and subsequent radiative cascade. The resulting Halpha/Hbeta and Hgamma/Hbeta ratios follow a different trajectory from dust reddening, allowing the two effects to be distinguished using multiple Balmer lines. In unresolved systems, a cool source located near the line-emitting gas may provide an additional radiation field distinct from the hot stars responsible for ionization. Balmer decrements may therefore carry information about otherwise hidden components of the radiation field surrounding the emitting gas.
item.dc:creator: Maryam Dehghanian, Fransisco Guzman, Peter van Hoof, Chamani Gunasekera, Gary Ferland

item.title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
item.description: arXiv:2610.12729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($\epsilon_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($\Sigma_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $\epsilon_{\rm ff}-\Sigma_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $\epsilon_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log \Sigma_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Escamilla, Michael Y. Grudi\'c, Anna L. Rosen

item.title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.12743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.
item.dc:creator: Lis\'an David Cabrera-Gonz\'alez, Carlos C\'ardenas, Otoniel Denis-Alpizar

item.title: Decomposing the Kinematics of SNR G180.0-01.7 with Medium-Resolution Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.12880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exceptionally large angular diameter and intrinsic optical faintness of the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G180.0-01.7 (S147) have historically hindered a comprehensive spectroscopic census of its filamentary structure. We present the first dedicated medium-resolution (R ~ 7500) spectroscopic study of S147 using the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic survey of Galactic Nebulae (MRS-N). By implementing multi-Gaussian decomposition on the H$\alpha$, [NII], and [SII] emission complexes and applying combined spectroscopic and spatial criteria, we disentangle the shock-ionized filaments of the SNR from the pervasive foreground and background Diffuse Ionized Gas (DIG). Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal radial velocity distribution for the SNR: a low-velocity population tracing the decelerated forward shock at a dense cavity wall, and a high-velocity population (with absolute radial velocities of ~ 70 $\pm$ 30 km/s) corresponding to ejecta within a low-density cavity. The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$\alpha$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.
item.dc:creator: Juan-Juan Ren, Wei Zhang, Chao-Jian Wu, Chao Liu, Jian-Jun Chen, Hong Wu

item.title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214
item.description: arXiv:2610.13039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($\Delta v=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($\Delta v=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($\Delta v=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($\Delta v=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.
item.dc:creator: Shulan Yan, Taotao Fang, Xiaochuan Jiang, Junfeng Wang, Qingzheng Yu, Chuanpeng Zhang, Ming Zhu

item.title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
item.description: arXiv:2610.13062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.
item.dc:creator: Lachlan Marnoch, Stuart D. Ryder, Sunil Simha, Alexa C. Gordon, R. M. Shannon, Nicolas Tejos, Marcin Glowacki, Ziteng Wang, Elizabeth K. Mahony, J. Xavier Prochaska, Wen-fai Fong, Richard M. McDermid

item.title: The Population of Type~1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
item.description: arXiv:2610.13218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a spectral analysis of a large sample of low-redshift type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). For objects at $z\le0.9$, we perform spectral fitting and ML-assisted refinement, yielding 114,754 type 1 AGNs. We use two fitting schemes that differ only in the broad-line model: the broad Balmer components are fitted with either a Lorentzian function or a sum of Gaussians. The continuum and [O III] luminosity measurements agree closely between the two schemes, whereas the Gaussians scheme generally yields larger broad-H$\beta$ full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, larger virial black hole masses, and lower accretion rates. The adopted broad-Balmer profile also changes the decomposition of narrow Balmer emission. Specifically, the anti-correlation between [O III]$\lambda5007$/narrow H$\beta$ and accretion rate is stronger under the Gaussians scheme with a Spearman rank correlation coefficient $r_{\rm s}=-0.412$, than under the Lorentzian scheme with $r_{\rm s}=-0.206$; the same tendency is observed in the narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) subset ($r_{\rm s}=-0.435$ and $-0.259$ for the Gaussians and Lorentzian schemes, respectively), suggesting that the Gaussians scheme may provide a more self-consistent separation of the broad and narrow H$\beta$ components. Moreover, the consistent correlations recovered under both profile prescriptions favor a continuous type 1 accretion-state sequence, with NLS1s occupying its high-accretion end rather than constituting a distinct population.
item.dc:creator: Zhu-Heng Yao, Wei-Jian Guo, Shuo Zhai, Yu-Chang Li, Cheng Cheng, Jun-Rong Liu, Shuang Jin, Antonios Katsianis, Jing Wang, Da-Wei Xu, Jian-Yan Wei

item.title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [OIII] Emission Filament
item.description: arXiv:2610.13329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report [O\,\textsc{iii}] narrow-band imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the SWONS (Super Wide-Field [O\,\textsc{iii}] Narrow-band Survey), together with multi-fiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H$\alpha$, [N\,\textsc{ii}], [S\,\textsc{ii}], and [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2,684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities (RVs), and full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs). The [S\,\textsc{ii}]/H$\alpha$ ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O\,\textsc{iii}] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O\,\textsc{iii}] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O\,\textsc{iii}] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of $\sim$160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of $\sim$28 pc along the north-south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O\,\textsc{iii}] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Fei Wu, Songyu Jia, Chao-Jian Wu, Chao Zhang, Li-Yue Zhang, Shu Wang, Juan-Juan Ren, Quzhen Dongyang, Hong-Yun Qiu, Zhi-Hong He, Jichen Zhang, Guo-You Sun, Wei-Guo Zhang, Jian-Jun Chen, Hong-Liang Yan, Xiang-Song Fang, Hong Wu

item.title: High Resolution Spectro-Polarimetric Observations of the Optical Filaments surrounding NGC 1275 with ESPaDOnS
item.description: arXiv:2610.13719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze archival high spectral resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetric observations (R = $\lambda/\Delta\lambda$ = 68000) of three targeted locations within the filamentary nebula surrounding NGC 1275. We present here the analysis of the main filaments emission lines, namely: [NII]$\lambda6584$, H$\alpha$, and [NII]$\lambda6548$, across our three pointings displaying clear detectable emission, with one also showing additional [SII]$\lambda6716$ and [SII]$\lambda6731$ emission line doublet. Using a Markov Chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) algorithm and thanks to the exceptionally high spectral resolution of the observations, we resolve for the first time each of the emission lines within one of the pointings into a set of three emission components with a remarkable velocity dispersion contrast ($\sigma_1 \sim 25$ km/s, $\sigma_2 \sim 90$ km/s and $\sigma_3 \sim 208$ km/s). We also perform flux ratios of the three detected emission components, which reveal differences in electron density and ionization sources. Consequently, the ESPaDOnS observations appear to reveal for the first time the overlap of an outer quiescent filament and a central turbulent filament likely affected by the AGN activity at a distance of $\sim 6.8''$ ($\sim 2.5$ kpc) from the central BCG. Finally, ESPaDOnS polarimetric data of one of the pointing allows us to confirm an average linear polarization degree of $\sim 0.15-0.14\%$ and an angle of polarization of $5.3\pm25.7^\circ$ for the optical emission of the filaments, as well as polarization dips associated with the H$\alpha$ emission line and its multiple emission components. We interpret these features and measurements as tentative polarization due to dust scattering.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Vigneron, Julie Hlavacek-Larrondo, Luca Fabiani, Lison Malo, Carter Lee Rhea, Megan Donahue, Jorge Karolt Barrera Ballesteros, Hyunseop Choi, Nadine Manset

item.title: Turbulence modes in molecular clouds in M33: a challenging test of the Brunt-Federrath framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.13726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the turbulent structure of molecular clouds is essential for linking galactic environment to the regulation of star formation. Although Galactic molecular clouds have been studied extensively, extending turbulence-mode analysis beyond the Milky Way remains challenging because of the limited spatial resolution and dynamic range of extragalactic observations. We assess the applicability of the Brunt \& Federrath (2014; BF14) framework to molecular clouds in M33. We apply BF14 to 128 $^{13}$CO(2-1) clouds, selecting a primary quality-controlled sample of 54 clouds and a more restrictive 25-cloud subsample defined using a stricter extraction-padding criterion (PAD=2) for quantitative analysis.Tests of cloud and noise power spectra, Fourier-space cutoffs, extraction padding, and Monte Carlo uncertainties demonstrate that the retained spatial frequencies are dominated by astrophysical signal and that the inferred turbulence-mode fractions are robust against reasonable analysis choices. Both samples yield consistent distributions of the solenoidal fraction, with mean values of $R \simeq 0.22$ for both samples and median values of $R \simeq 0.18$ and $0.17$, respectively, indicating that compressive motions dominate the turbulent energy budget. No strong systematic variations of $R$ are found with galactocentric distance or tracers of recent star formation. These results demonstrate that, despite the challenging spatial resolution of current extragalactic molecular-line observations, the BF14 framework can be applied reliably to nearby galaxies using spectroscopic observations alone. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first application of the full BF14 formalism to extragalactic molecular-cloud observations.
item.dc:creator: Raffaele Rani, Ayu Konishi, Kazuyuki Muraoka, Toby J. T. Moore, David J. Eden, Karan Fernandes, Yueh-Ning Lee, Shih-Ping Lai

item.title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous $z>2$ quasars
item.description: arXiv:2610.13742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We aim to provide a cookbook for purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and to provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous $z>2$ quasars. We analyse the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. We show that the proper motion signal to noise $\mu/\sigma_{\mu}$ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking into account the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopt the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled $\chi^2$ distribution with $k=2$ and scale $s=1.1485$ is fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding $\pm2\sigma$ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is $D^2_{M(\mu)}<7.097$. The final criteria combine this with the parallax condition and $\mathrm{ruwe}<1.4$. Applying the new criteria to the SDSS DR16Q confirmed quasars, the recovery rate is $90.25\%$. The suggested purely astrometric selection significantly improves both completeness and purity compared to other strategies used in the literature, reaching a quasar purity of approximately $95\%$ ($\sim2\sigma$ Gaussian-equivalent). It can be used to improve the selection purity and completeness for future quasar surveys. As an example, we use the suggested strategi to locate 24 very bright $z>2$ quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95\% of known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries is demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous $z>2$ quasars. Ten of these are new discoveries and for an additional seven we correct the redshifts determined by other methods.}
item.dc:creator: J. Li, J. P. U. Fynbo

item.title: A dust-reddened quasar in a [C II]-luminous host at z=6.55
item.description: arXiv:2610.13758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most known quasars at $z>6$ were selected through their rest-frame UV emission. Only a small number of reddened quasars have been identified at these redshifts, leaving their nuclear and host-galaxy properties poorly constrained. We present JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA band 6 observations of the quasar J1440+0019 at $z=6.5488$, revealing its dust-reddened nature and jointly characterizing its nucleus and host galaxy. The continuum is best described by an SMC-like extinction law with $E(B-V)=0.20\pm0.03$. Three absorption systems detected in N V, Si IV, and C IV are blueshifted by approximately $900$--$3600$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely trace an ionized nuclear outflow. The broad Mg II line and extinction-corrected continuum yield a black-hole mass of $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=9.04\pm0.42$, a bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.1\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and an Eddington ratio of $\lambda_{\rm Edd}\simeq0.8$. ALMA observations further reveal its host galaxy to be among the most [C II]-luminous known at $z>6$, with $L_{\mathrm{[C II]}}=(7.21\pm0.25)\times10^9 L_\odot$. For a fiducial dust temperature of 47 K and emissivity index $\beta=1.6$, the dust continuum implies $L_{\rm TIR}=8.9\times10^{12} L_\odot$ and $M_{\rm dust}=4.0\times10^8 M_\odot$. The inferred dynamical mass places J1440+0019 in the region of the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm dyn}$ plane occupied by high-redshift blue quasars. These observations reveal a moderately reddened, rapidly accreting quasar in a luminous, dust-rich host during reionization. Its measured nuclear and host-galaxy properties provide an observational reference for identifying and characterizing similar systems in future systematic searches with wide-area infrared surveys.

item.title: Insights from the stability of methanol maser flare properties I: G9.62+0.20E
item.description: arXiv:2610.13774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The brightest 6.7 GHz methanol maser in the Galaxy is associated with the high-mass star-forming region (HMSFR) G009.62+0.20E. Additionally, this methanol maser shows periodic flaring observed at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Several models have been hypothesized to explain the periodicity, including periodic accretion, spiral shocks in the gaps of circumbinary disks, pulsating stars, dicke's superradiance, and a colliding wind binary (CWB) system. We analyzed the time series of the 1.22 km s-1 feature of the 6.7 GHz methanol maser spectrum and the 1.25 km s-1 feature of the 12.2 GHz methanol maser spectrum over the monitoring duration of roughly 20 years, to determine an updated period, analyze the stability and repeatability of the flares, the temporal behavior of the flare profile, and the duty cycle of the flare profile based on the updated period. From these results, it is argued for or against any of the mechanisms that have been proposed to explain the periodicity. Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods were used to determine the methanol maser period at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Once the period has been determined, phase-folding or period-folding was used to analyze the flare shape, flare stability, and duty cycle of the flares. The periods of the 6.7 and 12.2 GHz methanol masers were determined to be ~ 243.0 +- 0.3 days. The flares are highly repeatable, stable, and show almost identical shapes, as well as their duty cycles. A replicated kernel density estimator (KDE) of the flare shape reproduces the time series very well over a time span of ~ 8000 days. After careful consideration of the proposed mechanisms for periodic methanol masers, we conclude that all but one, the CWB model, have been ruled out as a possible driver of this flare profile. It has also been established that the CWB model can qualitatively explain the flare profile of the periodic methanol masers.
item.dc:creator: S. P. van den Heever, D. J. van der Walt

item.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
item.description: arXiv:2610.13920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emission-line galaxies provide key diagnostics of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. We present a systematic census of emission-line sources using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) from the COSMOS-3D program, which covers a large contiguous area of 0.33 deg$^2$ and provides F444W grism spectroscopy over $3.9$--$5.1\ \mu$m. By combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging data, we construct a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of 12,275 objects at redshift 0--9. The typical $3\sigma$ line-flux limit reaches $3.2\times10^{-18}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$. To address source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy, we develop a multi-step identification framework that combines information from spectra, images, spectral energy distributions, and spatial distributions. We introduce convolutional neural network and large language model to emulate the human identification process and improve efficiency. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for all sources. The F444W WFSS enables the detection of multiple emission lines, including primarily [O III], H$\alpha$, He I $\lambda10830$, [S III] $\lambda\lambda9531,9069$, Pa$\beta$, Pa$\alpha$, Br$\beta$, PAH, Br$\alpha$, allowing a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. We construct composite spectra in several redshift bins and detect a variety of faint spectral features that are difficult to identify in individual spectra, including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and [Fe II] lines. This catalog provides a key reference dataset for studies of galaxy evolution and AGN activity, and demonstrates the power of WFSS for constructing large, unbiased spectroscopic samples over wide areas. The full catalog will be publicly available online upon publication.
item.dc:creator: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang, Jie Chen, Linhua Jiang, Chenxi Bao, Yihe Wang, Ronaldo Laishram

item.title: Galaxy Clustering Can Reveal Host-Galaxy Properties of Binary Black Hole Mergers
item.description: arXiv:2610.11045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Galaxy clustering encodes information about the host galaxies of binary black hole (BBH) mergers even when individual hosts remain unidentified, because the distribution of neighboring galaxies depends statistically on the host-galaxy population. We construct event-level host-type likelihoods from host-conditioned galaxy-count distributions within gravitational-wave localization regions and combine them to infer the fractions of BBH mergers hosted by different galaxy populations. The framework applies to common and rare galaxy populations without prescribing formation efficiencies or merger delay-time distributions. Using measured star-forming and quenched galaxy clustering, idealized one-year forecasts assuming all mergers occur in quenched galaxies yield median one-sided 90% lower credible limits of 0.19, 0.48, and 0.92 on the quenched-host fraction for O5, post-O5, and third-generation networks. These forecasts illustrate the potential for host-galaxy population inference before the third-generation detector era.
item.dc:creator: Daiki Watarai, Hayato Imafuku, Fumihiro Chuman

item.title: An Ultraviolet Instrument on the Habitable Worlds Observatory: Considerations and Capability Trades on the Multi-Object, Integral-field, and High-resolution modes of a potential UVI
item.description: arXiv:2610.12974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is NASA's next-generation astrophysics platform, delivering transformative capability in the search for life and study of the origins of the universe. Amongst the instruments under consideration for HWO is a multi-purpose ultraviolet spectrograph and imager that provides a deep toolbox for some of the most pressing science investigations of the next several decades. In this paper, we present a basic draft model of a potential UVI, including a multi-object spectrograph, far ultraviolet imager, high resolution spectrograph, and integral-field spectrograph. The draft designs for these channels of the UV instrument serve as a basis for a general discussion of the instrument architecture and design challenges, while also identifying potential trades, enhancements, and other considerations that the HWO project will need to address as it moves into the formulation phase. We conclude with a presentation of several scientific simulations that have helped guide the capabilities of the draft design. This paper is intended to serve as a summary of UV instrument modes, technology, and potential design ahead of planned instrument studies in the late 2020's, and then Phase A in the early 2030's.
item.dc:creator: Brian Fleming, Kevin France, Dmitry Vorobiev, Jeanette Donber, Eric Frater, Thomas Delker, Vicki Herde

item.title: X-Shooter view of planetary nebulae microstructures I: The case of NGC 7009 knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.13587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The properties of NGC 7009 knots are investigated by employing UV-to-near-infrared data from the X-Shooter spectrograph. These structures belong to the category of low-ionization structures (LISs), which are characterized by enhanced emission from low-ionization species and whose origin remains enigmatic. Our main goal is to conduct the first dedicated spectroscopic study of LISs using X-Shooter, that covers a wide spectral range from the UV to the near-IR, simultaneously. As a pilot study, we focus on NGC 7009 to investigate its ionized, atomic, and molecular gas, aiming to better characterize the physical properties of its LISs and explore their largely unexplored molecular content. The spectrum was processed through the ESO Reflex pipeline, and the physical properties of LISs were derived with the latest version of PyNeb. More than 250 emission lines were detected in the spectra of NGC 7009 LISs, including rare, forbidden transitions from low- ionization species such as Fe+ and Ni+, as well as two transitions from P+, identified here for the first time in LISs. The detection of multiple shock tracers, together with the shock excitation of [Fe II] and [O I], as revealed by emission-line diagnostics, supports the presence of shocks at LISs. The richness of the spectrum allowed us to derive electron temperatures and densities at the LISs using both collisionally excited and optical recombination lines. In the near-IR spectrum of the LISs, nine ro-vibrational H2 emission lines were detected, seven of which were reported here for the first time. These lines were used to construct the H2 excitation diagram, providing new insights into the physical conditions of the nebular gas. The excitation of molecular hydrogen is most likely dominated by collisional processes through shocks.
item.dc:creator: L. Konstantinou, S. Akras, K. Bouvis, P. Boumis, J. Garcia-Rojas, D. R. Gon\c{c}alves, K. N. Gourgouliatos

item.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2610.13942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To search for very wide-orbit binary-lens events, we cross-match microlensing events detected by OGLE-IV and KMTNet between 2011 and 2024. After removing contaminants from variable stars, we identify OGLE-2016-BLG-0523 as a microlensing event showing two short-lived bumps in its light curve, with the two separated by 8.36 yr. We investigate three scenarios to explain the two bumps, including a binary-lens single-source (2L1S), a single-lens binary-source (1L2S), and two unrelated single-lens single-source events (2$\times$1L1S). The 1L2S interpretation is excluded due to its poorer fit to the data, while the 2$\times$1L1S scenario is disfavored by the low event rate, unphysical total source flux, and unphysical color for one of the two putative sources. For the surviving 2L1S interpretation, the Einstein timescales of the two bumps are $8.343 \pm 0.076$ days and $3.231 \pm 0.047$ days, respectively, implying a binary mass ratio of $q = 0.15$. A Bayesian analysis indicates that the primary lens is most likely a low-mass M dwarf, while the companion is probably a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter. The inferred projected separation is about 450 au, making the companion the widest low-mass object discovered via microlensing to date. Our discovery highlights both the promise and challenges of identifying very wide, low-mass companions through microlensing. Although upcoming facilities such as Roman and Earth 2.0 space telescopes will improve sensitivity to such events, overcoming degeneracies and distinguishing them from variable phenomena will remain essential for building a robust statistical sample.

item.title: On the relation between magnetic field strength and gas density in the interstellar medium. II. Density uncertainties and diffuse gas constraints
item.description: arXiv:2603.06838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The relationship between magnetic field strength and gas density is essential to understand the interstellar medium and star formation. Zeeman measurements in dense atomic and molecular gas phases have traditionally been used to directly probe magnetic field strengths in the Milky Way. This allowed derivation of a relationship between magnetic field strength $B$ and gas number density $n$. We recently generalized this relation as a two-part power-law with non-zero slopes and a transition density given as $B/B_0 \propto (n/n_0)^{\alpha_1}$ for $n \le n_0$ and $(n/n_0)^{\alpha_2}$ for $n > n_0$. Here, we extend our previous hierarchical Bayesian framework by incorporating a large body of pulsar observations that probe the diffuse interstellar medium and explicitly modelling density uncertainties through a log-density intrinsic scatter $R_n$ applied to all densities. We also account for magnetic field geometry and measurement uncertainties through a magnetic hyperparameter to estimate $B$. This results in a stronger constraint on the diffuse gas part of the $B$--$n$ relation. Our results confirm a non-zero exponent in the diffuse gas and a broad transition density with our best model and data set yielding maximum a posteriori results of $\alpha_1 = 0.20^{+0.01}_{-0.03}$, $\alpha_2 = 0.65^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$, $n_0 = 3330^{+270}_{-3220}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$, and $B_0 = 10.11^{+0.71}_{-5.97}\,\mu\text{G}$.

item.title: Far-infrared Polarization Properties of Nearby Star-forming Regions: A New Compendium of SOFIA/HAWC+ Observations
item.description: arXiv:2603.09962v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comprehensive polarimetric study of 26 nearby molecular clouds in four far-infrared bands (53 $\mu$m~to 214~$\mu$m) using 52 archival SOFIA/HAWC+ datasets{, over half of which are unpublished}. Far-infrared dust polarization observations probe the plane-of-sky magnetic field. To investigate scale-dependent trends, we group the molecular clouds by distance and analyze the data at common angular ($25''$) and common physical (0.052 pc and 0.32 pc) resolutions. The two shorter wavelengths are more impacted by smoothing, exhibiting a larger decrease in percent polarization. We analyze the polarization spectrum --- the polarization fraction as a function of wavelength --- and find that it depends more strongly on column density than dust temperature. We find a ``falling" spectrum at the 0.052 pc resolution, but find a ``flat" spectrum at the 0.32 pc resolution, suggesting that resolution plays an important role in the observed polarization spectra. We propose that warm dust grain emission in small-scale structures ($\lesssim$~0.1 pc) traces different magnetic field geometries only resolved in our {near} regime data. There is no preferred magnetic field orientation across our data, which suggests that the magnetic field in our $\sim$~parsec scale regions is decoupled from the large-scale field that is primarily parallel to the Galactic plane. The relationship between percent polarization and column density varies between clouds, but the correlation between percent polarization and {polarization angle} dispersion is consistent across regions. This compendium highlights the value of observing at multiple far-infrared wavelengths and enables additional population-level studies of magnetic fields and dust across star-forming environments.
item.dc:creator: Kaitlyn Karpovich, Susan E. Clark, Enrique Lopez-Rodriguez

item.title: ID-MAGE II: The Star Forming Satellites of Low-Mass Hosts
item.description: arXiv:2603.18973v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present results from our ongoing campaign to follow up the satellite candidates from the Identifying Dwarfs of MC Analog GalaxiEs (ID-MAGE) survey. Previously, we published a list of 355 unresolved satellite candidates identified around 36~nearby LMC- and SMC-mass hosts (D$=$4$-$10~Mpc). We present the velocities of 83 satellite candidates from new Green Bank Telescope HI observations, optical long-slit spectra, and the Dark Energy Survey Instrument Data Release 1. Based on their velocities, we identify six candidates as probable satellite galaxies ($6.5\times10^5\leq M_\star/M_\odot\leq1.5\times10^7$) and 77 as background galaxies. Our results underscore the ability of spectroscopic follow-up to effectively separate satellites from background galaxies. Using the refined sample, we update our previously derived estimates for the average satellite population per host and find 1.7$\pm$0.7 (1.0$\pm$0.3) satellites per LMC-mass (SMC-mass) host. Our current satellite sample includes 25 galaxies confirmed by distances or velocities. This set includes the complete satellite populations of three hosts (UGC~04422: zero satellites, UGC~08201: zero satellites, NGC~3432: four satellites), which we compare to simulations and known satellite systems from the literature. Our sample is nearly complete for the most massive satellites (M$_\star > 10^7~M_\odot$). We find these massive satellites have a quenched fraction of 10--25\%, placing them between the $<$5\% quenched fraction of isolated galaxies and the 40--70\% quenched fraction of MW-analog satellites with $10^7~M_\odot < $ M$_\star < 10^8~M_\odot$. This demonstrates the impact that low-mass galaxies have on the evolution of their satellites.

item.title: Observing the Peculiar Acceleration of our Solar System with Quasar Proper Motions
item.description: arXiv:2605.30367v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We measured the proper motion dipole of quasars observed by \textit{Gaia} to determine the acceleration of the Solar System with respect to the quasar rest frame. We characterised the full angular power spectrum of the proper motion field using the pseudo-$C_\ell$ formalism and employed simulation-based inference to jointly constrain the dipole and higher multipole power. Cross-correlation with the \textit{Gaia} scanning strategy, stellar density and stellar proper motion maps was used to diagnose the origin of systematic power beyond the dipole. We applied this framework to both the \textit{Gaia} EDR3 quasar catalogue and the Quaia catalogue. The inferred acceleration is consistent with the previous determination, but the credible intervals widen by factors of 1.5 to 5 when higher-multipole degeneracies are properly marginalised, indicating that previous uncertainty estimates were optimistic. Our best estimate, based on the Quaia catalogue, is ($g_x,\,g_y,\,g_z$) = $\left(1.01^{+0.72}_{-0.72}, \,-4.94^{+0.54}_{-0.55},\,-2.13^{+0.58}_{-0.58}\right) \;\rm \mu as \,yr^{-1}$. This corresponds to an amplitude of $5.55_{-0.53}^{+0.54}\,\rm \;\mu as\,yr^{-1}$, where $\mathbf{g} = \mathbf{a}/c$ is the Solar System acceleration expressed as a proper motion drift in equatorial coordinates. The inferred acceleration is directed towards $(l,\, b) = \left(11.71^{+7.0}_{-6.8},\, -9.01^{+7.0}_{-6.9}\right)^\circ$, equivalently $(\alpha,\, \delta) = \left(281.39^{+7.8}_{-8.0},\, -22.93^{+6.5}_{-6.2}\right)^\circ$. This is in good agreement with a Galactic centre--dominated acceleration. The acceleration components show no significant dependence on source redshift, providing further evidence of the acceleration's kinematic origin.
item.dc:creator: Phu Huy Nguyen, Calum Murray

item.title: Reduced incidence of little red dots at z < 3 based on number density and halo mass evolution
item.description: arXiv:2606.02773v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An intriguing puzzle in extragalactic astronomy is the scarcity of Little Red Dots (LRDs) at $z < 3$, compared to their higher abundance at earlier cosmic epochs. To investigate this, we measure the overdensity for 98 specpically confirmed LRDs at $3<z<7$, and find that these LRDs predominantly reside in under-dense regions at $z > 4$ but shift to more typical galaxy environments at $z \sim 3.5$. Concurrently, cross-correlation analyses show that their dark matter halo masses grow rapidly, from $\lesssim 10^{10.1} \, M_{\odot}$ at $z \sim 7.5$ to $\sim 10^{11.3} \, M_{\odot}$ at $z \sim 3.5$, approaching the halo masses of normal galaxies at lower redshifts. Applying an empirical stellar-to-halo mass scaling relation, we find that LRDs still host over-massive black holes relative to their stellar masses at $z > 4$, yet converge toward the local BH-stellar mass relation at lower redshifts. The coherent evolution of LRDs' large-scale environments and halo masses toward those of normal galaxies provides a plausible explanation for their declining abundance at $z < 3$, even though the underlying small-scale physical mechanisms remain elusive.
item.dc:creator: Chenxuan Zhang, Huanian Zhang, Qingwen Wu, Luis C. Ho, Jian-Min Wang

item.title: The FAST HI 21-cm Absorption Blind Survey. III. OH Absorption Search in the 21-cm Absorber Sample and Continued HI Absorption Search
item.description: arXiv:2607.15595v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first blind search for OH 18-cm absorption with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST), conducted alongside the HI 21-cm absorption search. Our previous FAST blind HI absorption search identified 34 systems. In this work, we extend the search using 2024 and part of the 2025 CRAFTS and FASHI data (394.4 hr and 1622.1 deg$^{2}$) together with FATHOMER observations, yielding four known and three new HI absorbers, for a total of 41 HI absorption systems. We search for OH absorption in 19 HI absorption systems whose OH redshifted frequencies fall within the FAST band. The known OH absorber towards PKS 1413+135 was re-detected, making our survey the first blind survey to detect OH absorption. No new OH absorbers were identified. We examine the relationship between $N_{\rm{OH}}$ and $N_{\rm{HI}}$, applying survival analysis to account for upper limits. The analysis does not provide statistically significant evidence for either an $N_{\rm{OH}}$-$N_{\rm{HI}}$ correlation or redshift evolution of $N_{\rm{OH}}$/$N_{\rm{HI}}$. Finally, spectral stacking sets 3$\sigma$ OH column density upper limits of 4.93, 1.64, and 1.72 $T_{\rm{ex}}$/$c_{\rm{f,OH}}\times$10$^{12}$cm$^{-2}$K$^{-1}$ for associated, intervening, and combined samples, corresponding to [\rm{OH}]/[\rm{HI}] ratios of $<$1.66$\times$10$^{-8}$, $<$1.42$\times$10$^{-8}$, and $<$0.90$\times$10$^{-8}$, assuming $T_{\rm{ex}}$=10K for OH and $T_{\rm{s}}$=100K for HI. These results place the strongest constraints to date on the OH content in radio-selected HI absorbers and establish a blind-survey benchmark for future studies of molecular gas in HI-selected systems. They also demonstrate that known HI 21-cm absorbers provide an effective parent sample for systematic OH absorption searches, paving the way for future larger surveys.
item.dc:creator: Wenkai Hu, Yougang Wang, Jeremy Darling, Zheng Zheng, James R. Allison, Elaine M. Sadler, Wenxiu Yang, Yichao Li, Yidong Xu, Jie Wang, Fengquan Wu, Di Li, Ming Zhu, Xuelei Chen

item.title: Infrared spectroscopy of gas-phase hydrogenated and methylated pyrenes: from laboratory spectra to the simulated 3.4 $\mu$m emission band
item.description: arXiv:2607.16018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Observations of the aromatic infrared emission band at 3.3 mic often reveal satellite emission features in the 3.4 - 3.6 mic range. While the 3.3 mic band is attributed to the CH stretching vibration of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the satellite bands - particularly its prominent 3.4 mic component - is assigned to aliphatic CH stretching vibrations in hydrogenated and methylated PAH-like species. Our aim is to derive state-of-the-art infrared emission spectra for aliphatic-containing pyrene derivatives and compare them with astronomical observations. This will help refine our understanding of the contribution of these species to the 3.4 mic emission band. Mid-infrared spectra (1.4-25 mic of gas-phase dihydropyrene, tehtrahydropyrene, hexahydropyrene methylated pyrene, and pyrene were recorded at temperatures ranging from 373 to 673 K, depending on the species. The band profiles were analyzed using a multi-component fitting tool, and empirical anharmonicity laws were derived to quantify the evolution of the band positions and widths with temperature. The obtained spectral data was combined with the results of a Monte Carlo emission model to simulate the emission spectra following UV-photon absorption, up to the dissociation limit (<6 eV). The resulting synthetic spectra were compared with James Webb Space Telescope observations of the Orion Bar region (PDRs4All program). Based on these state-of-the-art simulated spectra, we show that 1,2,3,6,7,8-hexahydropyrene matches all the constrains to fit the red component of the 3.4 mic band observed at 3.403 mic. While 1-methylpyrene may also contribute to the underlying emission plateau, its lack of a strong infrared band complicates detection in observed spectra, unlike hexahydropyrene. All experimental spectra and their temperature-dependent analyses are available in the new cosmicPAH-IRDB database.
item.dc:creator: Karine Demyk, Christine Joblin, Louan de Bentzmann, Dominique Toublanc, Giacomo Mulas

item.title: Breaking the Blend: A multi-tracer kinematic decomposition method for IFS data applied to disentangling the AGN outflow and circumnuclear ring in NGC 5728 with JWST
item.description: arXiv:2609.30232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integral field spectroscopy (IFS) of the central kiloparsecs of active galactic nuclei (AGN) reveals a mixture of spatially coincident emission from star-formation and AGN feedback exciting the interstellar medium. Disentangling these components remains a challenge, as most spectral tracers are affected by both processes, limiting robust interpretation of kinematics and energetics. We present a new framework for decomposing IFS data into distinct components on a spaxel-by-spaxel basis using a multi-tracer, stacked kinematics approach. This method combines kinematic modelling with imposed flux decomposition per spaxel, quantifying the contribution of each component across the field of view. We apply this method to JWST IFS observations of the Seyfert galaxy NGC 5728 from the Galaxy Activity, Torus, and Outflow Survey (GATOS), analysing twelve mid-infrared fine-structure lines (4.49 < $\lambda$ < 25.89 $\mu$m, 7.9 < IP < 126.2 eV). We find that the circumnuclear emission can be decomposed into two dominant components: a star-forming ring and an AGN-driven biconical outflow. Our method separates these structures and recovers their detailed spatial morphology. This framework provides a general and scalable method for physically motivated component separation in IFS data, applicable across many wavelength ranges and targets, enabling reliable interpretation of complex emission line structures (or morphologies) in active galaxies and beyond.

item.title: Mass Proxy Quality of Halo Properties in IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO Simulations: II. Galaxies, Stars, and Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.10901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the stellar, black hole, and satellite galaxy populations of group- and cluster-scale halos in the IllustrisTNG, TNG-Cluster, and FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. We characterize the mass-conditioned scaling relations, covariance, conditional likelihoods, and mass proxy quality (MPQ) of integral properties within $R_{\rm 500c}$: total stellar mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm tot}$), brightest central galaxy stellar mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm BCG}$), intracluster light mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$), total black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$), satellite occupation ($N_{\rm sat}$), and satellite velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{\rm sat,\,1D}$), at $z\in \{0,0.5,1,2\}$. While normalization differences of up to a factor of two emerge among simulations, many properties exhibit remarkably similar mass-localized slopes, intrinsic scatters, and MPQs across halo samples and redshifts. Correlations among stellar, satellite, and gas properties are generally consistent in sign and their dependence on halo mass and redshift, whereas those involving $M_{\rm BH}$ and $N_{\rm sat}$ show greater variation, particularly in TNG-Cluster. Conditional likelihoods are nearly lognormal for many properties, including $M_{\star,\,\rm tot}$, $N_{\rm sat}$, and $\sigma_{\rm sat,\,1D}$, while $M_{\star,\,\rm BCG}$ and $M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$ are negatively skewed. Among the properties considered here, total stellar mass is the best mass proxy, with a halo mass scatter of $7$-$14\%$, followed by $N_{\rm sat}$ with a mass scatter of $9$-$18\%$. The consistent correlation behavior of $M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$ highlights its potential for next-generation observational studies. Finally, $\sigma_{\rm sat,\,1D}$ exhibits highly consistent scaling, with mass-independent slope and scatter and a largely neutral correlation structure, suggesting that it is relatively insensitive to astrophysical complexity.
item.dc:creator: Eddie Aljamal, August E. Evrard, Arya Farahi, Dylan Nelson

item.title: Beyond diagonal approximations: improved covariance modeling for pulsar timing array data analysis
item.description: arXiv:2506.13866v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) searches for nHz gravitational-wave backgrounds (GWBs) typically model time-correlated noise by assuming a diagonal covariance in Fourier space, neglecting inter-frequency correlations introduced by the finite observation window. We show that this diagonal approximation can produce method-dependent shifts in estimates of spectral parameters, especially for pulsars with shallow intrinsic red noise spectra. To address these limitations, we present a method that (i) computes the time-domain autocorrelation on a coarse grid using a fast Fourier transform (FFT), (ii) interpolates it accurately to the unevenly sampled observation times, and (iii) incorporates it into a low-rank likelihood via the Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury identity. Using both analytic covariance comparisons and end-to-end simulations inspired by the NANOGrav 15-year dataset, we demonstrate that our method captures frequency correlations faithfully, avoids Gibbs ringing, and yields estimates closer to the injected values in the realization studied with modest computational cost. As PTA datasets increase in sensitivity and complexity, our approach offers a practical and scalable path to fully accurate covariance modeling for current and future analyses.
item.dc:creator: Marco Crisostomi, Rutger van Haasteren, Patrick M. Meyers, Michele Vallisneri

item.title: From cosmological simulations to binary black hole mergers: The impact of using analytical star formation history models on gravitational-wave source populations
item.description: arXiv:2601.20202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Observations of binary black hole (BBH) mergers provide a unique window into the lives of massive stars across cosmic time. Connecting redshift-dependent merger properties to massive star progenitors requires accurate models of cosmic star formation and chemical enrichment histories. Analytical fits for the metallicity-specific cosmic star formation rate density S(Z, z) are commonly used as proxies for the complex underlying star formation history, yet they remain unconstrained. Using the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulations, we evaluate the accuracy of these analytical S(Z, z) prescriptions. By coupling the simulated and analytical S(Z, z) to the population synthesis code COMPAS, we investigate the resulting BBH merger rates and mass distributions. We find that analytical S(Z, z) prescriptions can overestimate BBH merger rates at high redshift ($z\gtrsim6$) by up to a factor of $10$-$10^4$, depending on cosmological simulation resolution, and can introduce spurious features in the BBH mass distribution. For example, they can produce an artificial feature near $8\,M_\odot$ in the primary mass distribution at $z\lesssim2$, which is absent when using the full simulation-based S(Z, z), while simultaneously suppressing high-mass features. These discrepancies arise because simple analytical models fail to capture a high-metallicity bump and a more flattened low-metallicity tail in the simulated S(Z, z) metallicity distribution. Our results highlight the importance of accurate star formation histories for modeling BBH populations, demonstrate the limitation of widely used analytical S(Z, z) fits, and underscore the need for careful integration of cosmological simulations, analytical fits, and population synthesis when interpreting gravitational-wave observations.

item.title: A possible detection of gas rotation in galaxy groups via the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
item.description: arXiv:2603.14494v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We utilise the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect (kSZ) to measure the rotation of ionised gas within galaxy groups defined in the SDSS-DR7 galaxy sample, via their dipolar imprint on the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We estimate the direction of the projected angular momentum for each of our selected fast-rotating groups by measuring the redshift dipole of satellite galaxies around their group centres. We find a clear redshift dipole in the stacked data for the selected SDSS groups. We then perform oriented stacking of the Planck CMB temperature map using the group centres and directions of angular momenta. We report a $2.3\sigma$ tentative detection of the dipolar rotational kSZ effect (rkSZ) within the virial radii of our fast-rotating groups from SDSS with an average mass of $10^{14}h^{-1} \rm M_{\odot}$ (corresponding to a null-hypothesis probability of 0.96%). We estimate the averaged rotational velocity of the sample to be $\sim 100-200 ~\rm km ~s^{-1}$, reaching a maximum value of $158.8\pm13.6 ~\rm km ~s^{-1}$. Our results are consistent within the errors with predictions based on the ELUCID constrained realisation simulation, with the predicted amplitude of the rkSZ signal being slightly lower near the centre. We also identify a systematic bias when estimating rotational velocities using the observed redshifts of galaxies, but find it to be subdominant for our analysis.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Yang, Yan-Chuan Cai, Weiguang Cui, John A. Peacock, Romeel Dav\'e, Houjun Mo, Huiyuan Wang, Xiaohu Yang

item.title: Carbon in J0815+4729: Casting a shadow of doubt on the interpretation of CH absorption in the most primitive stars
item.description: arXiv:2608.26731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Aims. We revisit the carbon abundance in the primitive iron-poor star J0815+4729 ([Fe/H] = -5.49). J0815+4729 is so carbon-enhanced and oxygen-rich that, in addition to CH and C2 molecular lines, weaker neutral atomic transitions are measurable in its spectrum, providing a unique opportunity to explore the line formation of C I and O I transitions in such an extremely iron-deficient star. Methods. Based on high-resolution spectroscopy and newly constructed atomic models for carbon and oxygen, we present the first investigation to derive carbon and oxygen abundances of this hyper iron-poor star from neutral atomic transitions under non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) conditions. Results. The carbon abundance derived from C I lines is A(C)NLTE = 8.08+-0.07, consistent with that inferred from C2 lines (A(C)LTE =7.96 +- 0.08), but around 0.6 dex higher than the value from CH lines (A(C)LTE = 7.47 +- 0.17). Since CH lines are the most commonly-used carbon abundance indicator for extremely metal-poor stars, this result casts doubt on the quantitative interpretation of CH absorption in the most primitive stars. We confirm that J0815+4729 is one of the most carbon-enhanced stars with [Fe/H] <= -4.5 known to date. We have also determined A(O)NLTE as 7.25 +- 0.11, with NLTE corrections of around -0.11 dex. The carbon-to-oxygen ratio of the star is [C/O] = 1.06 +- 0.1.
